### Observed At main `ac1876d7036190f3d8e53ed3a4453c78aee46e49`, the [push-triggered Deep run](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/actions/runs/45482911462) waited about 11h24m and 11h45m for its first two assignments. Node 22/npm and Node 26/Bun then passed in 18m01s and 12m57s. The other two lanes were cancelled at 11:10:11 UTC on November 25 with no runner or steps. They never ran; this is not a test failure. One second earlier an [ordinary scheduled Deep run for the same exact SHA](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/actions/runs/45601892659) entered the workflow. The replacement has no terminal coverage yet. [The exact workflow](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/ac1876d7036190f3d8e53ed3a4453c78aee46e49/.github/workflows/ci-deep.yml#L1-L27) uses one ref-level concurrency group and `cancel-in-progress: true` for push, schedule and manual events. That configuration plus the same-SHA run timing is consistent with automatic supersession; I did not independently verify the cancellation actor. The practical result is a matrix reset before any evidence for two compatibility lanes, after two other lanes already consumed compute. ### Acceptance - A same-SHA scheduled wake during an active push matrix must not cancel it merely to redo that commit. Coalesce, skip the duplicate, or let the admitted matrix finish without creating an unbounded backlog. - Keep a deliberate policy for a truly newer SHA and manual runs. Preserve post-merge Deep as observational, the four compatibility lanes and existing hosted fallback/PR requirements; do not create another heavy job. - Verify with a lightweight workflow/config test plus the next natural overlap (or isolated minimal fixture): unfinished lanes retain a chance to run, and a mixed cancelled matrix is never counted as full coverage. Related original quick/deep split: [`ops-ci-v2`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/ac1876d7036190f3d8e53ed3a4453c78aee46e49/.agents/pm/tasks/ops-ci-v2.toon).
